problems: The card never says the notification must stay inline, synchronous, when the sender belongs to the current thread. Only the cross-thread case is deferred. Reviewers treated this as essential: the normal same-thread case must still produce exactly one immediate disconnectNotify(), and Reviewer 15's QDBusAbstractInterface analysis depends on it.

The card leaves the dead-thread case vague. It says 'unless that thread can no longer deliver events' but never says what happens then. The merged code skips the notification entirely when the sender's thread has no event dispatcher; it does not fall back to a direct call. The QObject::disconnectNotify() docs were updated to say it 'is not called at all' in that case. Reviewer 10's suggested direct-call fallback was resolved by documenting instead, so an engineer reading the card might add the unsafe direct call.

The third bullet ties the external callers of QObjectPrivate::disconnectNotify() (qtdeclarative QQmlNotifierEndpoint, qtscxml) to this change. Reviewer 15 only asked whether to update that private helper and whether QtQml needs its own fix. The merged change leaves QObjectPrivate::disconnectNotify() and those external users untouched, so they are out of scope. The documentation that was actually added concerns the public QObject::disconnectNotify() and the new internal helper, not those callers.

The card omits an essential point Reviewer 15 required: reading the sender's QObjectPrivate from another thread is safe only because the caller holds the receiver's signalSlotLock. The sender's ~QObject() must take that lock to remove the still-present connection, so the sender cannot get past ~QObject(). The lock does not hold back the further-derived destructors. The card also omits that this ordering must be kept: notify before removing the connection from the sender's list.
